blocks.content:
Article 165 provides for Advocate General.

Key Points:
• Highest legal officer of the State
• Appointed by Governor
• Qualification: Judge of High Court
• Right to speak but not vote in Legislature

items: Frequently asked: The Advocate General has the right to speak in the Legislature, but has NO right to vote.
Match key provisions: Article 165 is associated specifically with the Advocate General of the State.
Qualifications check: A candidate must meet the qualification criteria for a Judge of the High Court.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 165 provides for the Advocate General of the State.
The Advocate General serves as the highest legal officer of the State.
The Governor is responsible for appointing the Advocate General.
To qualify for the role, a person must be eligible for appointment as a High Court Judge.
The Advocate General possesses the right to speak in the State Legislature, but cannot vote.
